children: Spic Brasil, a subsidiary of China's State Power Investment Corporation, has signed a contract with a Chinese consortium to expand the Sao Simao hydroelectric plant for 1.4 billion reais ($272.30 million), the power generator said on Thursday.

• The consortium, comprising Dongfang Electric Corporation and China Gezhouba Group, won a competitive process run by Spic for the 310-megawatt expansion awarded at Brazil's capacity auction in March.
• With the new unit expected to begin commercial operations in 2030, the plant located on the Minas Gerais-Goias state border will exceed 2 gigawatts of installed capacity.
• The March auction was the first opportunity in several years for new hydroelectric projects in Brazil.
• Optimization of existing assets is the most efficient and sustainable way to expand the country's renewable and secure energy capacity, Spic Brasil CEO Adriana Waltrick said in a statement.
